Emergency & Disaster Nursing

Emergency and disaster nursing — emergency codes, triage, disaster management, mass casualty incidents.

🎯 After this chapter you can

  • Describe emergency codes and their meanings
  • Explain triage systems and categories
  • Describe nurse’s role in disaster management

In simple terms

Emergency and disaster nursing involves responding to emergencies and disasters — from individual patient emergencies to mass casualty incidents. Nurses must know emergency codes, triage systems, and disaster response protocols.

Common emergency codes

Code Meaning Nurse’s action
Code Red Fire Rescue, Alarm, Confine, Extinguish (RACE)
Code Blue Cardiac/respiratory arrest Start CPR, call resuscitation team
Code Pink Infant/child abduction Secure exits, search, alert security
Code Silver Violent person/weapon Call security, do not confront alone
Code Black Bomb threat Follow evacuation instructions
Code Orange External disaster Prepare for mass casualties
Code Grey Combative person Call security, do not confront alone

Triage systems

Triage category Colour Definition Treatment priority
Immediate Red Life-threatening, treatable Immediate
Delayed Yellow Serious but stable Delayed
Minimal Green Minor injuries Delayed/walking wounded
Expectant Black Dead or expectant Palliative care only

Disaster management

  • Disaster phases — mitigation, preparedness, response, recovery
  • Mass casualty incident (MCI) — incident command system (ICS), triage, treatment, transport
  • Nurse’s role — triage, treatment, transport, documentation, psychological support

🔴 Triage categories

Triage categories (START system): Red = Immediate, Yellow = Delayed, Green = Minimal, Black = Expectant/deceased.

Where the nurse uses this

  • Emergency response — know emergency codes; know your role in Code Blue, Code Red, Code Pink, Code Silver
  • Triage — assess and categorize patients using triage categories; prioritize care based on acuity
  • Disaster response — participate in disaster drills; know your role in the incident command system
  • Mass casualty — triage, treat, transport; document patient information; coordinate with other agencies
  • Patient education — teach disaster preparedness, emergency preparedness, first aid

🔴 Most important for exams

  1. Emergency codes: Code Red (fire), Code Blue (cardiac arrest), Code Pink (infant abduction), Code Silver (violent person), Code Black (bomb threat), Code Orange (external disaster).
  2. Triage categories: Red = Immediate, Yellow = Delayed, Green = Minimal, Black = Expectant.
  3. Code Blue = cardiac/respiratory arrest; start CPR, call resuscitation team.
  4. Code Pink = infant/child abduction; secure exits, search, alert security.
  5. Code Silver = violent person/weapon; call security, do not confront alone.

⭐ Important for exams

  1. Disaster phases: mitigation, preparedness, response, recovery.
  2. Incident command system (ICS) = standardized approach to incident management.
  3. Mass casualty incident (MCI) = incident where resources are overwhelmed.
  4. START triage = Simple Triage and Rapid Treatment.
  5. Disaster nursing roles: triage, treatment, transport, documentation, psychological support.

📌 Memory trick

Triage categories: RIM-B — Red (Immediate), Yellow (Delayed), Green (Minimal), Black (Expectant).

60-second revision

  • Emergency codes: Code Red (fire), Code Blue (arrest), Code Pink (infant abduction), Code Silver (violent person), Code Black (bomb threat), Code Orange (external disaster).
  • Triage categories: Red = Immediate, Yellow = Delayed, Green = Minimal, Black = Expectant.
  • START = Simple Triage and Rapid Treatment.
  • Disaster phases: mitigation, preparedness, response, recovery.
  • Nurse’s role in disaster: triage, treat, transport, document, support.

Test yourself

Code Blue means:

Answer: B. Code Blue = cardiac or respiratory arrest; start CPR and call resuscitation team.

Code Pink means:

Answer: B. Code Pink = infant or child abduction; secure exits, search, alert security.

Red triage tag =

Answer: A. Red = Immediate = life-threatening but treatable; treat first.

Black triage tag =

Answer: D. Black = Expectant = dead or expected to die despite treatment; palliative care only.

Disaster phases include:

Answer: A. Disaster phases: mitigation, preparedness, response, recovery.
